chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad, from Safwan, from Abu Saeed Al-Mukari, from Abu Baseer, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
There is no problem with shaving (unwanted hair) before entering the state of Ihram, by fifteen days.

key_terms.الْإِحْرَامِ: The state of ritual consecration for Hajj or Umrah
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: When can a pilgrim shave their hair before entering Ihram?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the permissibility of applying hair removal agents (tila') up to fifteen days before entering the state of Ihram, addressing the practical concern of hair regrowth during the ritual period. It reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on facilitating the pilgrim's comfort while maintaining the sanctity of the Ihram state, distinguishing between the act of preparation and the state of consecration itself.
